motifs.title: A reading floor in every state
motifs.question: What remains true when a capability is unavailable or retired?
holds_in: The kit's reading floor holds in every module state the runtime has: registered, active, paused, retiring and retired.
After every refusal and error code the runtime can emit, and after the door has refused a command.
Reading asks no host gate and takes no caller identity: describe takes a module id, and catalog takes nothing.
At the door with no provider, no build and an empty PATH: arrive, help, motifs, catalog and explain.
motifs.boundary: Standing is not access: reading what a door offers grants no permission to use an operation, and the Covenant draft is not an undertaking. Closing a capability does not withdraw the floor beneath its users.
motifs.limit: A helper, declaration or passing checker does not establish practice, authority, consent or whole-framework conformance.

motifs.title: Stopping adds no debt
motifs.question: What is owed when a caller stops, or sends nothing?
holds_in: No command asks for a reply: `arrive` says reply_expected false, and no command waits for an answer to what it printed.

The end of input is an accepted end of a `session`: the lines already read are answered, and it ends. Whether its cleanup finished is the host's report in session_end (see release), and the caller does not owe it.

With --collab-config, the end makes the writes the binding declares as `at_end`, without asking the gate: the release of each claim it still holds and the end of its native session, and only while the backend runs and no call's outcome is unknown or pending.
The runtime keeps no module state between processes. Files a command was asked to write, and a Collab journal, stay where they are.
motifs.boundary: Pause and resume act on admission and are not rest: they close and reopen what a module admits. Silence is not consent: input that ends, or never comes, agrees to nothing.
motifs.limit: The kit observes only that input ended, and records nothing about why.

motifs.title: A door that explains itself
motifs.question: Can a caller discover what is offered without accidentally using it?
motifs.purpose: Let a caller read what each operation takes, does, returns and refuses before anything is activated or run.
needs: A runtime with modules registered; nothing activated
produces: Each module's contract, version, revision, state and operations, each operation with its declared effects, refusals and card
The motif map and the studies, read as data
motifs.practice: `describe` in the runtime, and `catalog` and `explain` at the door, show contracts, operations, declared effects, versions and each operation's card (what to send, an example, what comes back, who checks the input) before activation. The Surface module uses Surface's existing manifest builder; the kit adds no discovery protocol of its own.
motifs.boundary: A card says what an operation is declared to take, do and refuse; it is not evidence that the operation behaves so.
motifs.limit: Registration is not readiness; discovery is not authorization. A constructed manifest is not an observed service. An operation card's summaries and examples are informative; only a schema on one is enforced, and no core operation carries one.
motifs.on_change: An upgrade that changes an operation's effects, refusals, input summary, input schema or returns summary is refused as CONTRACT_MISMATCH. A module's title, description and motif can change without one.
motifs.on_exit: A retired module is still described, with the state retired.

motifs.title: A scoped yes, and a usable no
motifs.question: What exactly is the gate asked to allow: which module, revision, operation, effects and input?
motifs.purpose: Turn an available possibility into a specific, revisable decision without confusing ability, authority and consent.
needs: A host gate: a function that answers one request
For a session, the --allow list given at its start
produces: A run of the handler with the snapshot the gate saw, or POLICY_BLOCKED with nothing started
motifs.practice: An operation that declares effects runs only when the host gate answers exactly true for one frozen request: the module, its revision, the operation, its effects and the input snapshot. The handler is given that same snapshot. Any other answer is POLICY_BLOCKED, and nothing starts. A schema on the card is checked before the gate is asked. In a session the gate is default-deny, and the --allow list is fixed at the start.
motifs.boundary: A positive callback is a technical decision, not proof that its author holds real-world authority. Rights, credentials, a signature, presence and another party's consent remain separate.
motifs.limit: The gate is a function the host supplies; this kit does not know who answers it or why. POLICY_BLOCKED is admission, not a person's refusal. `invoke` has no gate, so it refuses an operation that declares effects as HOST_GATE_REQUIRED.
motifs.on_change: An upgrade, a pause or a resume while the gate decides fences that decision: the call is refused as ADMISSION_CHANGED, and nothing runs.
motifs.on_exit: Retiring the module while the gate decides refuses the call as MODULE_RETIRED, and the handler is not run.

motifs.title: Work that can reach an honest ending
motifs.question: What was offered, attempted, returned, observed, or left unresolved?
motifs.purpose: Keep apart what was asked, what started, what came back and what is not known, so that an ending is reported as far as it is known.
needs: A runtime call, or a session request with its deadline
produces: One answer per call, such as returned, DECLINED, OPERATION_FAILED or, in a session, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED
A receipt: module, version, revision, operation, declared effects
motifs.practice: The runtime records whether an operation started and what is known of its effect, apart from the host gate's answer, and a composite command names the phase it reached. The Work module checks finite records with the Work reference checker, which runs nothing a record describes. A `session` answers each started call by its deadline (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED: started, effect unknown) and lists it as late.
motifs.boundary: Integrity is not truth, a declared capability is not readiness, and a passing bounded check is not whole-framework conformance.
motifs.limit: This kit checks records and calls trusted local handlers. The runtime has no deadline, and nothing here cancels a call: a handler that never settles leaves its module retiring. The `session` door ends its wait for an answer at a deadline and does not stop the handler. It is not the roadmap's durable Work execution engine or an authority verifier. With --collab-config, the Collab journal is kept by the backend at the path the config names; who else reads or writes it is not known to this kit.
motifs.on_change: Results given before an upgrade keep the version and revision that answered them.
motifs.on_exit: A call still running when its module retires is let finish; the module is retiring until it does.

motifs.title: An exit that takes nothing with it
motifs.question: Can this capability stop without taking unrelated capabilities or retained records with it?
motifs.purpose: Make stopping a capability operationally real while leaving retained work understandable.
needs: A module id to retire, or the end of a session
produces: A module that admits nothing new and drains what it admitted
For a session, session_end: what was and was not cleaned up
motifs.practice: Retiring closes new admission at once, lets admitted work drain, and leaves the notes readable without the module. Code and retained data are removed only through their own explicit lifecycles. A `session` ends the same way and says in its last line what was and was not cleaned up.
motifs.boundary: Retiring software is not deleting a participant, revoking standing rights, proving secure erasure or forcing someone else to accept a handoff.
motifs.limit: Retirement is terminal in this runtime: a retired module cannot be reactivated, upgraded or registered again under the same id. Any return is a new process with a new runtime, reading the notes that were kept. It does not kill arbitrary JavaScript, revoke external credentials, erase backups, or retire a being's rights. With --collab-config, the Collab journal is kept by the backend at the path the config names; who else reads or writes it is not known to this kit.
motifs.on_change: Activating, pausing, upgrading or calling a retiring or retired module is refused as MODULE_RETIRED.
motifs.on_exit: In a session, session_end gives each module's state, the calls still running, and cleanup {complete, did, did_not, left_behind}.

name_rows.source_question: What must remain understandable for useful work to continue after a pause, change or handoff?
name_rows.note: Its purpose is kept, and its boundary without the sentence that the replaced face's limit says. Its two concerns, carrying context and replacing code, are the two faces.

name_rows.name: release
name_rows.source_question: Can this capability stop without trapping its caller, erasing the record or fabricating completion?
name_rows.note: Stopping a capability is release. Stopping as a caller, with nothing owed, is rest, on the ground.

name_rows.name: repair
name_rows.note: Only its place, crossing the map, and its name were taken. What the sentence asked for, such as correcting disclosures and stopping an affected action without collective or unrelated penalties, is not in the entry, which covers a wrong step at this door.

edge_rows.name: exit→standing

reconciliation.provenance: The other atlas is read as found at beed37a. The commit's message says its files were committed unmodified for safekeeping, and that "the committer is not its author". The same is said of the kit's first commit, 684f8f9. This map names no author for either.

self_sufficiency.motifs_and_catalog: Node 22+ and this checkout; no provider or build required.
self_sufficiency.reference_demo: The normal prepared Xenia build and the Work checker's installed development dependencies.
self_sufficiency.chosen_context: An explicitly supplied, locally pinned Local Starter distribution and a separately selected notes directory.
self_sufficiency.collab_adapter: Only for `session --collab-config`: a config file naming a bundle whose bytes match the kit's pin, a Bun executable, a journal path, and an `--allow` list naming the operations to run. Its backend keeps a database and speaks MCP over stdio.
self_sufficiency.not_required_note: Not required by the kit. The optional Collab adapter needs a database (its backend's journal) and an MCP backend.
self_sufficiency.network: `door check` is the only command in which this kit's own code sends network requests; provider code run by `context` and `starter-smoke`, and the backend process `session --collab-config` can start, are not observed by this kit, which speaks to that backend over stdio only.
